text:
maya: customers on hosted API complaining about repeated reconnects and a big spike in 502/503s during morning traffic window. several report duplicate billing entries.

aaron: timeline? any deploys or infra changes overnight?

maya: no deploys to runtime, but nginx ingress autoscaled up ~10 pods at 07:03 UTC and then we saw a reconnect surge starting 07:05.

priya: are these clients behind ALB/NLB/Cloudflare? which path?

maya: majority via our public ALB -> nginx ingress -> service. a subset via Cloudflare (worker) to ALB.

sam: can you paste a short log sample? interested in TCP half-close / keepalive messages.

maya: here's an example from ingress nginx: 
```
[2026-03-15T07:05:12Z] 10.2.3.45: connect fd 42 reused, upstream 10.4.1.23:443 closed, client closed connection, status 502
[2026-03-15T07:05:12Z] 10.2.3.45: unexpected EOF while reading body from client
[2026-03-15T07:05:12Z] 10.2.3.45: downstream socket timed out while waiting for client, closing
```

aaron: looks like we saw a bunch of upstream pod restarts or connection resets during the scale. nginx might be returning short 502s while backend drains. what about idle timeout mismatch?

maya: customer repro suggests long-running SSE streams idle for ~8m then client reconnects. ALB idle timeout is 600s (10m), nginx proxy_read_timeout default was 5m (300s) in our helm values.

priya: ah, mismatch. if nginx closes at 5m while ALB keeps the TCP conn open the client might not see immediate closure and then a reconnect storm when multiple clients time out their app-level heartbeat.

sam: also consider upstream keepalive pool: when pods scale down connections get reassigned and nginx may attempt to reuse staled keepalive sockets; that causes EOFs.

maya: customer repro steps that reproduced the issue locally with curl SSE: 
1) open 200 concurrent SSE connections through ALB to nginx -> service -> runtime
2) simulate idle (no events) for 6m 30s
3) send a small keepalive from runtime; nginx drops connection earlier at ~5m then ALB still holds on. clients attempt reconnect at ~6:30 and all reconnect at once -> burst -> 503s

aaron: can you paste the curl command?

maya: curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream?token=REDACTED"

maya: when I force nginx proxy_read_timeout to 650s and align it with ALB 600s (actually set both to 650s to be safe) the reconnect storm disappears in the test.

priya: interesting. So fix options:
- align proxy_read_timeout / keepalive_idle with ALB idle timeout
- add application-level heartbeat (lightweight SSE comment) at <5m intervals to keep sockets live
- adjust ALB idle timeout down or configure nginx to 601s to be slightly higher than ALB so ALB closes first to surface closure to clients

sam: for immediate mitigation we can roll a config bump to nginx: set proxy_read_timeout: 650s and keepalive_timeout: 650s. Also add a note to docs about deploying behind ALB/Cloudflare timeouts.

maya: also noticed Cloudflare worker had its own fetch timeout config around 600s and was returning no hints when origin closed.

aaron: for the billing duplicate issue: when clients reconnect without sending a last-event-id we may reprocess partial session. we should ensure idempotency on server side or emit a session token so resuming clients can avoid double-count. escalate to runtime team for dedupe on reconnect within Xs.

priya: opened an internal PR to change helm values and a postmortem note. PR: helm/charts/ingress/values.yaml bump proxy_read_timeout -> 650s.

oncall-bot: deploy-batch scheduled at 2026-03-15T07:45Z to update ingress config (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

maya: notes for support docs update: "If using ALB/NLB/Cloudflare + nginx ingress, ensure proxy_read_timeout and keepalive settings match or exceed upstream idle timers. Consider heartbeat events < 5m to avoid proxy idle closure."

sam: follow-ups: 1) short-term config roll, 2) add heartbeat helper in runtime SDK, 3) runtime idempotency for reconnects, 4) doc + customer outreach.

maya: customer notified of temporary mitigation and asking if we can whitelist their org for an immediate config canary.

aaron: approved. creating canary with tag org-whitelist for two customer clusters. will monitor 07:50–08:30 UTC. :eyes:

priya: adding playbook steps and a snippet to reproduce for support: 
```
# simulate 100 clients reconnecting after idle
for i in $(seq 1 100); do 
  (curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.../v1/stream?token=..." &) ;
done
sleep 390 # idle
# many clients will reconnect here
```

maya: thanks team. I'll attach customer logs and billing timestamps to the incident page.

sam: thanks — keep alerts up on 502/503 and reconnect rate. will follow up with runtime eng about dedupe windows.

maya: closing thread after deploy monitoring window unless we see regressions. :white_check_mark:
